mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized copy of passport for each director and UBO
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary Public in the director's country of residence

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Good Standing / Corporate Incumbency from the home country registry
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Home country Registrar of Companies or registered agent

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter or source-of-funds statement for the initial capital deposit

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory enhanced due diligence for all UBOs and directors against the Samoa FIU domestic list, OFAC SDN list, UN Security Council Consolidated List, EU restrictive measures, and SAMOA international companies register disqualification list. PEPs must undergo enhanced scrutiny including source-of-wealth and source-of-funds review. No nominee or corporate vehicle may be incorporated without completed screening and TRA/SIFA AML compliance sign-off.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Samoa International Companies Registry (operated by Samoa International Finance Authority, SIFA) - Online Name Reservation System
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Names must be written in English or Samoan using the Latin alphabet. If the proposed name is in a non-Latin script (e.g., Chinese characters), a standard transliteration into the Latin script and an English/Samoan approved equivalent must be submitted. The name must contain a corporate suffix such as 'Limited', 'Ltd.', or the Samoan equivalent.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant's registered agent may file a written request for reconsideration to the Registrar within 14 days from the date of rejection. If reconsideration is declined, an administrative appeal may be lodged with the Minister for Commerce and Labour within 30 days. The applicant may simultaneously re-submit a modified name. A rejected name remains restricted for 6 months, after which it becomes available for another applicant.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual office is not acceptable as the statutory registered office. An International Company must maintain a physical registered office and an active registered agent inside Samoa. For an intraocular lens manufacturing entity requiring a special license, the Samoan International Company must also demonstrate a substantive local presence should it conduct any regulated activities in Samoa; otherwise, the IC will be strictly offshore in activity and cannot rely on a virtual office to satisfy compliance.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 20% estimated risk of unannounced physical inspection by SIFA and/or FIU during the first fiscal year; for an ISIC 3250 high-risk medical device special license, the risk escalates to 35% if any Samoan operational presence is ever claimed.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: International Companies Act 1987 (as amended by the International Companies (Amendment) Act 2009), ss. 5-10 (incorporation procedure), s. 8 (share capital), s. 16 (registered office), ss. 31-38 (directors), s. 66 (secretary); Business Licences Act 1998 (as amended) for operational licensing
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA), Apia, Samoa
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Incorporation of an International Company (Form IC-01) together with executed Memorandum and Articles of Association, resulting in issuance of a Certificate of Incorporation
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; shares may be issued with or without par value and denominated in any currency (International Companies Act 1987, s. 8). No escrow account, capital contribution, or local bank account is required for incorporation.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED THAT the subscribers' share subscription be and is hereby ratified, and the Board shall allot and issue the subscribed shares of no par value upon receipt of agreed consideration; RESOLVED FURTHER THAT the registered office located at the licensed registered agent's office in Apia, Samoa be and is hereby adopted as the Company's statutory registered office under Section 16 of the International Companies Act 1987; RESOLVED FURTHER THAT [Name] be appointed Director and [Name] be appointed Secretary, each holding office until removed by resolution; RESOLVED FURTHER THAT the aforesaid officers are authorized to open banking accounts, execute banking mandates, and complete all filings necessary to maintain the Company's tax-exempt status.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of International Companies, Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA), acting through a SIFA-licensed registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name reservation request electronically via the licensed registered agent's portal. Confirm the proposed corporate name is not identical or confusingly similar to any name already on the International Companies Register and does not contain prohibited words (international companies act 1987, s. 6). The name is reserved for 30 days pending submission of the full incorporation application.
required_dossiers: Name reservation request form
Registered agent engagement letter
Beneficial owner due diligence/KYC declaration
Entity structure confirmation and proposed business purpose
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is refused on grounds of similarity or prohibition, submit up to three alternative names for re-screening; a formal written appeal may be lodged with the Registrar for administrative review within 14 days of the refusal notice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Execution of Constitutional Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: SIFA-licensed registered agent, with notarization before a Notary Public in Samoa or an authorized foreign notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Memorandum and Articles of Association in a form acceptable under the International Companies Act 1987, including objects clause, share provisions, director and secretary powers, and indemnity clauses. The subscriber(s) must execute the documents before a notary, and the registered agent must countersign its consent to act as registered office holder.
required_dossiers: Draft Memorandum and Articles of Association
Subscriber consent and signature pages (notarized)
Consent of registered agent to act
Certified copy of passport or ID of each subscriber
Proof of residential/professional address of each subscriber
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar's pre-filing review raises requisitions, amend the constitutional documents and re-execute the affected pages before a notary, then resubmit within 14 days to avoid expiry of the name reservation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of Incorporation Application and Statutory Declarations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registrar of International Companies, SIFA Registry Division, Apia
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File Form IC-01 together with the executed Memorandum and Articles of Association, the registered agent's consent, director and secretary consents, and the KYC/beneficial ownership pack. Payment of the government filing fee is made through the licensed registered agent. The application is lodged in duplicate; one certified copy will be returned with the Certificate of Incorporation.
required_dossiers: Form IC-01 (Application for Incorporation of an International Company)
Executed Memorandum and Articles of Association (duplicate)
Consent to act as director and secretary
Consent of registered agent and registered office address
Beneficial owner declaration and source of funds statement
Government filing fee remittance advice
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried for defective filing, cure the stated defect and resubmit the corrected Form IC-01 and exhibits within 14 days; the Registrar will process the corrected application within the original statutory period without re-imposition of the incorporation fee.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Payment of Fees and Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon validation of the application, the USD 100 government incorporation fee is applied, and the Registrar issues the Certificate of Incorporation under the official seal of SIFA, assigning a unique International Company number. The registered agent collects the certificate and certified constitutional documents.
required_dossiers: Acknowledgment of application receipt
Proof of government fee payment
Form IC-01 stamped filed by Registrar
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If certificate issuance is delayed beyond the statutory period, the registered agent may submit a written expedition request to the Registrar; where the delay is due to a registry error, a duplicate certificate will be issued at no additional cost.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Governance and Corporate Kit Formalities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of Directors, with administrative support of the licensed registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the first board meeting or pass the written first board resolution adopting the pro-forma resolution covering share allotment, registered office adoption, and officer appointments. Issue share certificates to members, open the statutory registers (members, directors, secretary, charges, and beneficial owners), and arrange for opening of corporate bank accounts and SWIFT/Letter of Credit facilities.
required_dossiers: First board resolution (written or minutes)
Share certificates and share register
Register of directors and secretary
Consent to act of each officer
Corporate bank account opening pack and banking resolution
Registered office certificate and agent acknowledgment
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the board resolution is challenged as procedurally defective, the directors may execute a unanimous written consent ratifying all acts taken in reliance on the resolution; corrected resolutions are re-issued with effect from the original date.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Statutory Filings and Annual Maintenance
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the notice of first directors and secretary with the Registrar within the statutory period, confirm the registered office address, and pay the annual government license fee on each anniversary of incorporation. Maintain the registered agent and registered office in Samoa at all times and file any subsequent changes of directors, secretary, or registered office within 30 days.
required_dossiers: Notice of directors and secretary (Form IC-04)
Confirmation of registered office and registered agent
Annual government fee remittance
Beneficial ownership confirmation return
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the company fails to pay the annual fee, SIFA will issue a warning notice; payment of the fee plus late penalty within 3 months avoids strike-off. A struck-off company may apply for administrative restoration within 7 years upon payment of arrears and reinstatement fees.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL) - Business Licence Registry, in coordination with the Samoa Bureau of Standards (SBS) for medical device quality systems and the Ministry of Health (MOH) Therapeutic Products Unit for medical device establishment oversight
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Medical Device Manufacturing Business Licence issued under the Business Licences Act 1998 (as amended), together with a Medical Device Establishment Manufacturing Certificate issued by the Ministry of Health for the production of intraocular lenses

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment (MNRE) - Planning and Urban Management Agency (PUMA)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category B: Controlled Activity - EIA Registration with an Environmental Management Plan (EMP); a Full EIA Report is not required absent significant hazardous effluents or discharge to sensitive coastal receptors
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater discharge to municipal sewer must comply with Samoa Water Authority discharge standards (BOD less than or equal to 300 mg/L, pH 6.0-9.0); solvent consumption (isopropyl alcohol cleaning agents) below 2 tonnes per annum keeps the facility below the VOC reporting threshold; polymer scrap and rejected lens inventory must be segregated and disposed of as scheduled non-hazardous waste under the Waste Management Act 2004 with disposal manifest records retained for audit

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire Safety Certificate from the Samoa Fire and Emergency Services Authority (SFESA) under the Fire and Emergency Services Act 2008 covering fire suppression systems and means of egress; building code and structural load clearance from PUMA under the Planning and Urban Management (Building Code) Regulations; workplace occupational safety and health registration and annual inspection with MCIL under the Labour and Employment Act 2013; ISO Class 8 cleanroom particulate certification for lens lathe-turning and finishing areas

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry for Revenue (MfR), Government of Samoa; Self Access Revenue System (SARS) portal at www.revenue.gov.ws
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-owned Samoa International Company (IC) is incorporated by a licensed registered agent with the Registrar of International Companies, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL), under the International Companies Act 1987 (as amended). Within 30 days of incorporation, the registered agent must lodge the Certificate of Incorporation, registered office consent, director and shareholder particulars, and specimen signature with the Ministry for Revenue (MfR) to obtain a Taxpayer Identification Number (TIN). For an IC that does not carry on business in Samoa, the MfR issues a TIN together with a Certificate of Tax Exemption confirming that the company is exempt from Samoan income tax, VAGST, stamp duty, and withholding tax. If the IC later elects to carry on business in Samoa, it must notify the MfR and obtain an amended tax registration as a resident commercial company.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Samoa does not provide a check-the-box or hybrid mismatch election akin to US Subchapter S or Treasury check-the-box rules. An International Company is statutorily exempt from all Samoan taxes while it does not transact business with residents of Samoa. The IC may elect in its constitution to prohibit bearer shares, may elect to merge or migrate into and out of Samoa under the International Companies Act, and may voluntarily elect to be treated as a resident trading company, in which case the standard 27% corporate income tax and VAGST regime apply. No CFC or hybrid mismatch election is available under domestic law.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAGST (Value Added Goods and Services Tax)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: WST 100,000 annual taxable turnover (mandatory registration); voluntary registration permitted below the threshold
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No national real-time e-invoicing, e-clearance, or digital stamping mandate is currently in force. Taxable persons must issue a valid VAGST invoice for every taxable supply and retain supporting records for seven years. VAT returns and payments are filed electronically through the MfR Self Access Revenue System (SARS), and customs export declarations are lodged electronically through the Samoa Customs electronic clearance system.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Exports of goods, including foldable hydrophobic intraocular acrylic lenses falling under ISIC 3250 / HS Chapter 90, may be zero-rated at 0% VAGST under Section 7 of the VAGST Act 2009 where the supplier exports the goods, directly or indirectly, in the course of a taxable business and the goods leave Samoa within 28 days of supply. The exporter must retain documentary proof that the goods were physically exported and sold to a non-resident customer; input VAT credits on attributable manufacturing inputs remain refundable. Offshore services supplied to non-residents who are outside Samoa at the time of supply are separately zero-rated where the territorial export test is satisfied.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Samoa Customs Export Declaration (CUSDEC) bearing customs endorsement
Commercial Invoice describing goods and stating 0% VAGST export treatment
Bill of Lading or Air Waybill evidencing physical removal from Samoa
Certificate of Origin (Form A or non-preferential certificate)
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank credit advice evidencing receipt of export proceeds in foreign currency
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The Ministry for Revenue may audit any zero-rated export claim and refund within a seven-year limitation period and recover any refund or input tax credit erroneously claimed together with default interest of 1.5% per month, a late payment penalty of 10% of the outstanding tax, and an additional penalty equal to up to 100% of the tax shortfall for evasion or intentional misstatement. Fraudulent zero-rating and refund claims are criminal offences punishable by fines of up to WST 10,000, imprisonment of up to five years, disqualification of the registered agent, revocation of the exporter's status, and a retrospective clawback of all benefits claimed with interest.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Samoa (CBS), also known as Faletupe Tutotonu o Samoa, exercising delegated exchange-control authority under the Exchange Control Act 1975 and the Exchange Control Regulations 1976 (as amended), with ultimate statutory oversight retained by the Minister of Finance.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Samoan Tālā (WST) is partially convertible: current-account payments for trade, services, and interest are liberally processed through authorized dealers, but all capital-account transactions require prior CBS exchange-control approval. Profit and dividend remittances by the WS_IC International Company are permitted only with a valid CBS permit, audited after-tax profit evidence, a tax-clearance certificate from the Samoa Ministry of Revenue, and confirmation that all exchange-control reporting obligations are current. The WS_IC is tax-exempt but must nevertheless demonstrate genuine commercial substance in the intraocular-lens manufacturing chain; remittances above the declared threshold are reviewed on a per-transaction basis by the authorized dealer and CBS.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Exporters must repatriate all export receipts through an authorized dealer within 3 months from the date of export, with 100% mandatory conversion into WST unless the CBS grants a Foreign Currency Retention Account exemption (typically restricted to funding trade inputs within 180 days). For the cataract-lens production line, each inward credit must be matched against the relevant customs export declaration; any shortfall, delay, or discrepancy must be explained in writing to the authorized dealer and is reportable to CBS on the monthly exchange-control return.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Settlement Account with Foreign Currency Savings Account and Authorized Dealer FX Facility

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Bank of South Pacific (Samoa) Limited (BSP Samoa)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational / Escrow Account with WST and USD sub-accounts and Trade Finance Line
Operational Account with Authorized Dealer FX Facility and Corporate Internet Banking
Domestic Operational Account (limited international wire capability)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low / not independently viable. Samoa does not license digital EMI entities, and offshore EMIs cannot provide WST-denominated accounts, domestic Samoan clearing, CBS reporting, or authorized-dealer FX functions. Offshore EMIs may serve only as secondary liquidity rails (e.g., USD pooled settlement accounts) after the primary local authorized-dealer relationship is fully established; any direct use of an EMI for Samoan FX transactions would violate the Exchange Control Regulations 1976.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical appearance is mandatory: at least one sitting director and every beneficial owner must attend an in-person Customer Identification Program (CIP) interview at the bank's Samoan branch; remote/electronic account opening is not permitted for offshore International Companies in this high-risk medical-device scope. All corporate documents must be notarized and apostilled (or legalized by the Samoa Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Trade), and the licensed Samoan registered agent must countersign the board resolution authorizing account opening.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Offshore tax-exempt International Company flagged as a letterbox entity with no economic substance or verifiable physical operations.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of incorporation and certificate of good standing; registered agent certification; notarized board resolution; audited financial statements or a licensed accountant's compilation report; physical production-site lease or laboratory contract in the operating jurisdiction; ISO 13485 certification; ophthalmic-device regulatory license; a written commercial explanation of the tax-exempt status and the actual lens-manufacturing activity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk medical-device trade flagged for trade-based money laundering through over/under-invoicing of intraocular-lens raw materials (hydrophobic acrylic monomers, lathe-cutting consumables).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Signed purchase orders and OEM supply agreements; CIF/FOB invoices; bills of lading and air waybills; HS-coded customs declarations; independent product valuation memorandum; raw-material laboratory test certificates; a gross-margin forecast aligned with industry norms; and bank-to-bank references from the home jurisdiction.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: UBO opacity, prior bearer-share issuance, or an undisclosed multi-layer Chinese-language beneficiary chain.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full share register disclosing natural-person UBOs; CBS-prescribed UBO declaration; notarized passport copies; recorded CIP interview notes; source-of-wealth and source-of-funds statements; sworn declaration that any bearer shares have been cancelled or effectively immobilized; and a sanction/PEP screening report for every director and UBO.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and high-jurisdiction procurement concerns over acrylic polymer supply chains routed through high-risk corridors.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: UN/EU/OFAC/UK consolidated sanctions screening reports; complete corporate ownership charts; end-user certificates for all ophthalmic raw materials; OEM supply contracts with customs declarations and export licenses from the home regulator; and correspondent-bank confirmation letters validating the source of goods and funds.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound equity capital requires prior CBS exchange-control approval and a Foreign Investment Certificate from the Samoa Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL); funds are transferred via SWIFT MT103 using purpose code 'Capital Injection / Equity Subscription' and must match the share-issuance resolution. The authorized dealer conducts source-of-funds verification and CBS counterparty screening before crediting; wires above USD 10,000 require bank call-back confirmation and are reported on the monthly exchange-control return, with funds initially lodged in a capital escrow/retention account pending final KYC clearance.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails comprise (a) SWIFT MT103 for cash trade settlements and operational disbursements; (b) Commercial Letters of Credit (sight or up to 120-day usance) issued by the Samoa dealing bank for OEM lens-component purchases, tooling, and packaging; and (c) documentary collections through the authorized dealer. Outbound FX transfers above USD 10,000 require a per-transaction exchange-control permit, supported by invoice, packing list, and transport documents; CBS monthly reconciliation is mandatory, and USD liquidity is sourced through the bank's international NOSTRO correspondents in Sydney or London.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable WST forward contracts (up to 12 months) with authorized dealer banks for documented commercial import/export cover
Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) on WST via offshore counterparties, executed only with prior CBS approval
Cross-currency swaps between WST/USD linked to the verified trade receivable and payable cycle, subject to CBS exchange-control permit
Currency-swap and forward-option combinations backed by underlying contracts, where CBS approval is obtained and the transaction is reported on the monthly exchange-control return

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return of a Samoa International Company
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) – Registrar of International Companies
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 30 calendar days after the incorporation anniversary date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty is charged from the first day of default; persistent non-filing for a continuous period may lead to show-cause proceedings, publication of intended strike-off, and administrative deregistration of the International Company.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual License Fee / Government Renewal Fee
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Payable on the incorporation anniversary date, or within the annual licensing window published by SIFA (typically between 1 June and 30 June for the following licence year)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: An additional late payment penalty is imposed after the deadline; continued non-payment of at least 3 months may suspend good standing and prompt strike-off from the International Companies Register. Reinstatement requires payment of arrears, penalties, and a government restoration fee.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Samoa International Company is exempt from a mandatory statutory audit unless its articles of association impose an audit, or shareholders holding at least 25% of the issued shares serve a written requisition requiring an independent auditor to be appointed.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS is permitted for voluntarily prepared financial statements, however a Samoa International Company is not required to file individual financial statements with SIFA unless an audit or shareholder requisition has triggered such obligation.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The registered agent must review beneficial ownership against the confidential UBO register at least annually and file changes arising from shareholding transfers within 21 days of the transfer being entered into the Register of Members. The SIFA beneficial ownership register is confidential and not publicly searchable.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,000 – USD 7,000 (only triggered by shareholder requisition, articles of association, or parent-group audit requirements)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% (standard resident company rate under the Income Tax Act 2012, effective for income years commencing on or after 1 January 2024; previously 27%); effective rate for a validly registered International Company is 0% by virtue of section 198 of the International Companies Act 1987.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Full ring-fenced exemption: an International Company is exempt from Samoan corporate income tax, stamp duty and exchange-control restrictions on its worldwide income and distributions, provided it remains validly registered, files its annual return and complies with the International Companies (Economic Substance) Amendment Act 2021 if engaged in a relevant activity. Manufacturing of intraocular acrylic lenses (ISIC 3250) attracts no Samoan income tax on export-manufacturing profits.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: International Company Annual Return (Registrar of International Companies, Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL) Online Registry Portal), filed together with the annual government fee schedule prescribed by the International Companies Regulations.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due on the anniversary of incorporation; the filing window closes 30 days after the anniversary date, or 30 days after the annual general meeting if one is held before the anniversary.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Exact legal name as shown on the Certificate of Incorporation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders: name must match the certificate; no translated name accepted.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Unique MCIL registration number assigned upon incorporation.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Cross-check against the registered agent's incorporation file.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Physical address of the registered office in Apia maintained by the licensed registered agent.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A P.O. box is insufficient; a physical street address is mandatory.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Name and counter-signature of the licensed registered agent (law firm or accounting practice in Samoa).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident directors cannot self-file; the Samoan agent must co-sign the return.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Item 5 - Authorized and Issued Share Capital
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Authorized capital, issued shares by class, and consideration paid.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State amount in the currency of incorporation (typically USD) and identify all non-resident beneficial holders.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Description of the business using ISIC classification; for this entity: high-precision manufacture of foldable hydrophobic intraocular acrylic lenses, ISIC 3250.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The declared activity must match the statutory medical-device manufacturing license and all export/LC documentation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration under section 198 of the International Companies Act 1987 that the company is exempt from Samoan income tax for the year.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Must be signed by a director; a false declaration triggers shortfall penalties and criminal liability.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Statement of whether the company carries on a relevant activity under the International Companies (Economic Substance) Rules 2021 (banking, insurance, shipping, fund management, financing and leasing, headquarters, holding company, intellectual property, distribution and service centre).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a pure lens manufacturer with no IP-licensing or distribution function, declare 'none of the above'; retain evidence of board meetings, premises and employee presence in Samoa.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing or non-payment of the annual fee attracts a late penalty of WST 200 plus interest at 10% per annum; default continuing beyond 3 months leads to administrative strike-off, vesting of assets in the Registrar, and a restoration fee of WST 1,000 together with all arrears.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% for an International Company: section 198 of the International Companies Act 1987 exempts the IC from all Samoan taxation, so dividends distributed to non-resident shareholders are not subject to Samoan dividend withholding tax. The general non-resident dividend withholding rate of 15% under Schedule 1 of the Income Tax Act 2012 is displaced for ICs.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Although IC distributions carry a 0% domestic rate, treaty relief under the Samoa-New Zealand and Samoa-Australia DTAs is documented as a backstop: (1) the non-resident beneficial owner obtains a Tax Residence Certificate (TRC) from its home tax authority, valid 12 months; (2) the beneficial owner submits the TRC and a completed treaty relief declaration to the IC's registered agent before the distribution date; (3) the agent files the declaration with the Samoa Ministry of Revenue (Commissioner of Inland Revenue) and obtains written confirmation where the gross distribution exceeds WST 100,000; (4) all supporting documents are retained for 5 years under the Tax Administration Act 2015. Treaty-reduced rates: dividends 15% portfolio / 5% for holders of at least 10% of the voting power; interest 10%; royalties 5%.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory non-resident withholding: interest 15%, royalties 15%. Treaty-reduced: interest 10%, royalties 5%. Where the intraocular lens manufacturer pays royalties to a non-resident for turning software or hydrophobic polymer IP, no Samoan withholding attaches because the IC is outside the Samoan income tax net; the payee's residence jurisdiction may still impose its own withholding.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Samoa Transfer Pricing Rules under the Income Tax Act 2012 and Tax Administration Act 2015: a Local File is mandatory where cross-border related-party turnover exceeds WST 10 million per income year; a Master File is mandatory where the multinational group's consolidated revenue exceeds WST 200 million. Below these thresholds, the IC must still retain a TP self-review matrix covering the lens-manufacturing intercompany margin and any IP or distribution functions.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The International Companies (Economic Substance) Amendment Act 2021 and the International Companies (Economic Substance) Rules 2021 impose an economic substance requirement on ICs carrying on relevant activities. Manufacturing of intraocular acrylic lenses (ISIC 3250) is not a listed relevant activity per se; however, if the IC licenses lens-design IP, holds an IP box, or performs distribution and service centre functions tied to the Samoan registration, ESR reporting applies and the IC must demonstrate: (i) a physical office in Samoa; (ii) at least one full-time employee or managing director in Samoa; (iii) board meetings held in Samoa; and (iv) proportionate local operating expenditure. A pure letterbox company is conclusively presumed to lack substance, and the tax exemption may be reversed.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax Evasion - False Exemption and Shortfall
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the IC to invoice intraocular lens manufacturing revenue that is in fact derived from Samoan domestic trading; filing false annual returns or false economic substance declarations; deliberately omitting export proceeds received via SWIFT Wire or Letter of Credit outside the declared ISIC 3250 scope.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Tax Administration Act 2015: a tax shortfall penalty of 150% of the avoided tax plus a fine of up to WST 100,000; criminal tax evasion carries imprisonment of up to 7 years on summary conviction or 10 years on indictment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and officers who sign false declarations are jointly and severally liable for the shortfall, penalties and civil restitution; the Commissioner may issue a departure prohibition order (travel ban) and freeze personal assets; conviction triggers director disqualification for up to 10 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company and Economic Substance Failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the IC as an empty shell with no Samoan office, no employees and no board meetings while passing lens-trading or IP income through the entity to claim exemption or treaty benefits; failure to file the economic substance declaration for a relevant activity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: ESR penalty of WST 25,000 plus WST 2,500 per month of continuing default; the Registrar may strike the IC off the register and treat the tax exemption as void for the income year in question.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Where the IC traded while insolvent or the shell was used to misrepresent beneficial ownership, directors are personally liable for the company's unpaid fees and penalties, are subject to disqualification, and may be imprisoned for up to 3 years for fraudulent trading.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML and Special-License Medical Device Trade
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: High-risk intraocular lens trade conducted without proper KYC and beneficial-ownership filing under Samoa's Money Laundering Prevention Act 2007; undisclosed commissions; use of cash or third-party shadow payment rails outside SWIFT Wire and Letter of Credit; invoice re-routing to obscure the ultimate hospital buyer.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: AML penalties of up to WST 500,000 per contravention; money-laundering predicate imprisonment of up to 14 years; revocation of the special medical-device manufacturing license and seizure of non-conforming products at the border.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and beneficial owners face asset seizure, personal fines equal to twice the value of the laundered proceeds, travel bans, mutual-assistance extradition and imprisonment for the predicate AML offence; compliance officers with knowledge are individually accountable.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the high-precision lathe turning of foldable hydrophobic cataract lenses without the required statutory medical-device manufacturing license administered by the Samoa Ministry of Health and without an export permit for the acrylic intraocular lenses.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Regulatory fines of up to WST 50,000 per unlicensed batch; seizure and destruction of non-conforming devices; suspension of the IC's annual registration and automatic loss of tax-exempt status for the affected income year.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The technical director and signatory directors are personally liable for fines, product recall costs and third-party compensation claims; criminal conviction carries imprisonment of up to 2 years and debarment from acting as a director in Samoa.
